Fix coverage of parallel builds and fill _adjust_url coverage gaps

- Collect coverage from Sphinx's parallel (-j) worker processes by
  enabling multiprocessing concurrency and parallel data files in
  [tool.coverage.run]. Previously, _adjust_url ran only in forked
  workers and was reported as never reached.
- Pass markdown_http_base and markdown_uri_doc_suffix in
  tests/test_builder.py without wrapping quotes. The arguments do not go
  through a shell, so the quotes became part of the config values.
- Build the overrides step with markdown_file_suffix=".markdown" to cover
  a custom file suffix in the diff tests.
- Cover same-document :doc: references and unreadable :download: targets
  in the test sources.
- Join markdown_http_base and the target URL with posixpath, so
  root-relative targets (e.g. /static/file.pdf) no longer produce a double
  slash (https://host//static/file.pdf).

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(tools): say when a private address is refused because private access is off

## Changes

When a download origin does not allow private addresses, the tool runtime
refused a private address with the message meant for addresses it never
contacts (link-local, cloud metadata, multicast, reserved). It now says that
private addresses are not allowed for this origin. Always-refused addresses
keep the existing message. `tool-runtime/src/tools/tabular/download.ts` only;
documentation is unaffected.

## Why

Follow-up to #1405, found in review. Every production origin allows private
access today, so users never see this message; the fix keeps the reason
accurate if an origin without private access is added.

## Planning

- Task: follow-up to #1405 (no issue)

## User-facing

No.

## Testing

- `bun test tests/tabular/download.test.ts`: 8 pass. The changed test failed
  first; it checks the private-access message with a local listener (zero
  connections) and the always-refused message for a multicast origin.
- `bun run typecheck`: clean.

## Accessibility

No UI change

Start the test tool servers outside the checkout so they read no .env

The tool server tests start `python -m openscientist_tools` from pytest's working directory, so in a deployed checkout the server's settings read that checkout's `.env`. The fixture already stripped the inherited `OPENSCIENTIST_*` variables but kept the directory. The `server_params` fixture now starts the server in an empty temporary directory, and the one test that starts the server itself runs it in its own temporary directory. A new test starts a process the way the fixture does from a directory holding a staging `.env` and checks it still sees the default executor image.

benchmarks.task_description:
Name a 24-bit downconversion without 16bit

Closes #1018

A source named `[WEB FLAC]` (24-bit files, no `24bit` in the name) downconverted to 24-bit/48 kHz was named `[WEB 16bit 24-48]`. For a 24-bit target with a sample rate, the FLAC word now goes straight to the `24-NN` token. 16-bit targets and `{resolution}`-only names are unchanged.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved output filenames for audio conversions when the source filename lacks a bit-depth label or a FLAC marker. 24-bit conversions now show the target resolution without an incorrect 16-bit label, while 16-bit conversions retain the appropriate FLAC label.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

benchmarks.task_description:
fix: type device_info as DeviceInfo for Home Assistant 2026.11

Unblocks #256 (homeassistant 2026.10.4 to 2026.11.0).

## What failed on #256
- **Quality gates:** 9 mypy errors. HA 2026.11 types `_attr_device_info` strictly, and plain dicts no longer match it.
- **build (Safety) and SonarQube:** both failed on an empty key. Dependabot runs get no repository secrets.

## Changes
- All `_attr_device_info` assignments in 6 entity modules now use `DeviceInfo(...)`. The values are unchanged.
- `safety-check.yml` and `sonarcloud.yml` skip their job when the actor is `dependabot[bot]`. Both still run on main after the merge.
  - Alternative: add `SAFETY_API_KEY` and `SONAR_TOKEN` as Dependabot secrets and drop the skip.

## Verified
- `./scripts/quality.sh all` with homeassistant 2026.11.0 installed: mypy and pyright clean, 1455 passed, 3 skipped.
- The change also works on 2026.10.4, since `DeviceInfo` exists there.

After this merges, comment `@dependabot rebase` on #256.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(api): recover milestones a slow event stream dropped

Fixes #15381

## Summary
A slow background event consumer could permanently skip durable milestones. Each subscriber queue is bounded, and a full queue drops its oldest frame. The tail only read durable storage during the initial replay or idle polling. So a surviving frame could move `Last-Event-ID` past milestones that were evicted but still persisted, and a later reattach started after them. Two related cases had the same result:
- When tokens evicted a milestone, the token exposed a newer cursor before that milestone was replayed.
- `close()` cannot queue its end marker into a full queue, so the stream could end without reading the last persisted event, or never end.

Per-job seqs are contiguous, so `InMemoryLiveBus.reattach` now treats a live frame past the next expected seq as a gap. Before it yields that frame, it reads the missing milestones back from durable storage, up to that frame's cursor, so token order and replay dedup are kept. A closed job ends once its queue is empty, after one final durable read. SSE framing and cursors are unchanged. Dropped tokens are not durable and are still not recovered.

## Testing
- New cases in `test_live_bus.py`, with the subscriber queue reduced to 2 frames as in the issue:
  - Milestones 2–4 published to a paused subscriber come out as `[2, 3, 4]` instead of `[3, 4]`.
  - Milestone 2 evicted by two tokens is yielded before them.
  - A job closed with a full queue ends, including a final milestone that was only persisted.
  - All three fail on the base branch.
- `src/backend/tests/unit/services/background_execution/` passes (87).

+

+class _DurableLog:
+    """A durable store the runner writes to before it publishes each milestone."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.frames: list[LiveFrame] = []
+
+    def persist(self, seq: int) -> LiveFrame:
+        frame = LiveFrame(seq=seq, data=f"milestone {seq}".encode())
+        self.frames.append(frame)
+        return frame
+
+    async def read(self, after_seq: int) -> list[LiveFrame]:
+        return [f for f in self.frames if f.seq > after_seq]
+
+
+def _token(seq: int) -> LiveFrame:
+    return LiveFrame(seq=seq, data=b"token", durable=False)
+
+
+async def _next(stream) -> LiveFrame:
+    return await asyncio.wait_for(stream.__anext__(), timeout=2)
+
+
+async def _rest(stream) -> list[LiveFrame]:
+    frames = []
+    while True:
+        try:
+            frames.append(await _next(stream))
+        except StopAsyncIteration:
+            return frames
+
+

+    for seq in (2, 3, 4):
+        await bus.publish("job-1", log.persist(seq))
+
+    assert [(await _next(stream)).seq for _ in range(3)] == [2, 3, 4]
+    await bus.close("job-1")
+    assert await _rest(stream) == []
+
+
+@pytest.mark.usefixtures("small_queue")
+async def test_reattach_recovers_a_milestone_tokens_evicted_before_yielding_them():
+    bus = InMemoryLiveBus()
+    log = _DurableLog()
+    log.persist(1)
+    stream = bus.reattach("job-1", last_seq=0, read_durable=log.read)
+    assert (await _next(stream)).seq == 1
+
+    await bus.publish("job-1", log.persist(2))
+    await bus.publish("job-1", _token(2))
+    await bus.publish("job-1", _token(2))

+    frames = [await _next(stream) for _ in range(3)]

[Harness] Том MLflow без external: docker compose up створює його сам

Closes #333 (M20). PR — проти `develop`.

**Проблема.** Після #329 том MLflow оголошено `external: true`, тож `docker compose up -d --build` в `aoi-demo/` падав на машині, де окремий стек ADS ще не створив `agentic-data-science_mlflow_data`: `external volume "agentic-data-science_mlflow_data" not found`.

**Що.**
- `ads.profiles.yaml`: `mlflow_data` — лише `name: agentic-data-science_mlflow_data`, без `external`. Compose створює том, якщо нема, і бере наявний том окремого ADS, якщо є: трасування обох стеків і далі в одному місці. Порожній том годиться — MLflow ADS тримає SQLite і артефакти в ньому.
- README: «Як це влаштовано» — демо створює том, якщо його нема; «Обмеження» — `docker compose down -v` у `aoi-demo/` тепер видаляє й цей спільний том (трасування ADS).

**Перевірка.** На машині без тому: `docker compose config -q` — ок; `docker compose up` — том створено compose (`com.docker.compose.project=aoi-demo`), `ads-mlflow` працює. Python не змінювався — гейт не запускався.

fix(agents): keep parallel tool results on their own run

Fixes #15380

## Summary
When an agent called the same tool twice in parallel with the same input, a result could land on the wrong step, and a tool error could disappear. The persisted message had the same problem as the live updates. `process_agent_events` keeps a map from each run to its `ToolContent` block, but every publication returns a new `Message` rebuilt from its dump, so those references went stale. `handle_on_tool_end` then picked the first block with the same name and input, and `handle_on_tool_error` wrote to a block that was no longer in the message.

Publications inside `process_agent_events`, including model rounds that publish while tools run, now rebind each run to the block at the same position. `content_blocks` only grows during a run. `handle_on_tool_end` completes the run's own block before it publishes, so the completion is in the publication that reports it. Handler signatures and message schemas are unchanged.

## Testing
- Reproduced with the event order from the issue: runs `a` and `b` of `search` with the same input, `b` finishing first. On the base branch, the outputs came out as `[result-b, result-a]`, and an error on `b` was lost.
- New cases in `src/lfx/tests/unit/base/agents/test_events_handlers.py`:
  - Model-declared and fallback-created blocks, each with `b` completing by success or error first. The run keeps its own result, and the publication for `b` carries its completion.
  - A model round published while both calls run keeps the error.
  - All five fail on the base branch.
- lfx agent, agent helper, and log boundary suites pass. On the backend side, `test_agent_events.py` and the OpenAI Responses tool-error and unstreamed-text suites pass (84).

+def _parallel_search_events(*, model_declared: bool, first_finished: str) -> list[dict]:
+    """Two calls to one tool with the same input; the second started finishes first."""
+    events = []
+    if model_declared:
+        two_calls = [{"type": "tool_use", "name": "search", "input": {}, "id": call} for call in ("a", "b")]
+        events.append({"event": "on_chat_model_end", "data": {"output": AIMessage(content=two_calls)}})
+    events.extend(
+        {"event": "on_tool_start", "name": "search", "run_id": run_id, "data": {"input": {"q": "same"}}}
+        for run_id in ("a", "b")
+    )
+    data = {"error": "error-b"} if first_finished == "on_tool_error" else {"output": "result-b"}
+    events.append({"event": first_finished, "name": "search", "run_id": "b", "data": data})
+    events.append({"event": "on_tool_end", "name": "search", "run_id": "a", "data": {"output": "result-a"}})
+    return events
+
+
+async def _run_recording_publications(events: list[dict]) -> tuple[Message, list[list[dict]]]:
+    published: list[list[dict]] = []
+
+    async def _send(*, message: Message, **_kwargs) -> Message:
+        dumped = message.model_dump()
+        published.append([block for block in dumped["content_blocks"] if block["type"] == "tool_use"])
+        return await Message.create(**dumped)
+
+    async def _event_iterator():
+        for event in events:
+            yield event
+
+    message = Message(content_blocks=[], sender="Machine", sender_name="AI")
+    return await process_agent_events(_event_iterator(), message, _send), published
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("first_finished", ["on_tool_end", "on_tool_error"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("model_declared", [True, False], ids=["model-declared", "fallback-created"])

+    """A run's completion lands on its own block, in the publication that reports it."""
+    events = _parallel_search_events(model_declared=model_declared, first_finished=first_finished)
+
+    result, published = await _run_recording_publications(events)
+
+    run_a, run_b = [block for block in result.content_blocks if isinstance(block, ToolContent)]
+    assert run_a.output == "result-a"
+    assert run_a.error is None
+    if first_finished == "on_tool_error":
+        assert (run_b.output, run_b.error) == (None, "error-b")
+    else:
+        assert (run_b.output, run_b.error) == ("result-b", None)
+    b_finished_alone = [

+        for blocks in published
+        if len(blocks) == 2 and blocks[0]["output"] is None and (blocks[1]["output"] or blocks[1]["error"])
+    ]

+

+    narration = {"event": "on_chat_model_end", "data": {"output": AIMessage(content="still searching")}}
+    events.insert(2, narration)
+

+
+    run_a, run_b = [block for block in result.content_blocks if isinstance(block, ToolContent)]
+    assert (run_a.output, run_b.error) == ("result-a", "error-b")

fix(frontend): create one flow on a repeated New Flow click

Fixes #16165

## Summary
A second click on **New Flow** while the first create was still in flight posted a second flow. Depending on timing, that left a spare "New Flow (1)" in the project, or showed "Flow creation error: Name must be unique" with the first flow created but never opened. `useStartNewFlow` now ignores clicks from the moment a create starts until the route changes, so one flow is created and its canvas opens. The hold covers the window after `navigate()` returns, since React Router commits the new route in a transition, and a failed create releases it so the button keeps working.

## Testing
- Reproduced with the issue's script against the base branch: with 300 ms of API latency and two clicks 100 ms apart, 4 of 6 runs stayed on the project page with the error toast. With a 600 ms create response and clicks 300 ms apart, 4 of 4 created two flows. With the fix, 10 of 10 runs created one flow and opened it, with no toast.
- New jest suite `use-start-new-flow.test.tsx`: a click while creating, and a click after the create but before the route changes, both create nothing. Both fail on the base branch. A failed create and a route change both let the next click create again. The flowBuilderWelcome and MainPage suites pass (915).
- New Playwright spec `tests/core/features/new-flow-double-click.spec.ts`: two clicks under API latency send one `POST /flows/` and open that flow. Locally it fails 3/3 on the base branch and passes 3/3 with the fix. The spec deletes the flows it creates.
